blind.why: Mid HUD-on (seed7, place 0,30) vs CS2 alley ss_4. CS2 has bounce-lit shade with readable texture and a clean grade. Ours has nice shafts, but the shaded walls go muddy brown, the shadows are soft and smeary, and the warm haze flattens the arch.

Long view vs Mirage ss_3. CS2 sand highlights hold detail and the grade is calm. Our sunlit sand nearly clips (p95 0.92), the shade sand is too bright, and the orange Ember bots sink into the orange walls. Close call.

B-tunnel vs Overpass ss_9. CS2 shows dark-to-light gradients and dappled shadow. Our roofed tunnel is evenly floodlit orange with no lamp pools, the floor is brighter than open-air ground, and the near-black pillars sit against it.
Tide-spawn vs Mirage arches ss_8. CS2 gets drama from crisp lattice shadows and value structure. Our spawn facade is one flat grey-beige shade plane with a sun flare on top and no depth layering.

biggest_gap: The interior ambient (skyocc) now floods roofed spaces, so interiors are brighter than sunlit exteriors. To reproduce: ?test=1&seed=7&match=1&phase=live, hide #ui, then ctx.map.debug.setView('b-tunnel'). The median luminance of the tunnel floor (x300-700, y400-540) is 0.72. The sunlit floor at 'catwalk' is 0.54 and the shaded floor there is 0.19. With render.debug.toggle('skyocc',false) the same tunnel floor is 0.22. The lamps give no pools or falloff: the whole corridor is uniformly orange-bright while the pillars stay near-black. CS2 keeps covered spaces clearly darker than sunlit ground, with local lamp pools and a gradient toward the openings. Fix: clamp the occluded ambient and floor-lift under ceilings to below exterior shade (about 0.6-0.8x). Make the lamp contribution a tight radial falloff (a pool radius of roughly 2-3 m) rather than a floor-wide lift, and let pillars receive the same fill.
other_gaps: Highlights run hot and the sun/shade spread on open ground is compressed. On 9 HUD-off frames, p95 is 0.87 vs 0.78 for CS2 and clipped pixels are 0.8% vs 0.1%. On long, sunlit sand is 0.86 and shade sand 0.70, so the ground reads as a pale, low-structure field (hub-arches, long, b-site foreground). Lower the sunlit albedo and exposure on sand/tile, or soften the ACES shoulder, and drop open-air shade fill slightly.

There is a milky bloom/haze veil over bright near-camera floors and the mid-distance (bottom third of hub-arches and b-site, the arch at mid). It reads as a lens smear rather than atmosphere. Raise the bloom threshold for diffuse surfaces and keep depth fog for distance only.

Saturation and warmth are about 1.6-2x CS2. Mean saturation is 0.43 vs 0.26 and R-B warmth is 0.20 vs 0.09. Orange Ember characters lose figure/ground separation against orange-brick and sand walls (long, mid). Pull global saturation and warm grade toward neutral and let the team colours carry the saturation.

Shaded facades are flat. At tide-spawn the whole wall is one grey-beige plane with no bounce, AO crease or value gradient, and the shaded walls at mid/b-site go muddy brown. Add per-face bounce/sky gradient (lighter low on the wall from ground bounce, darker under ledges).

Fine detail is soft: edge energy is 0.014 vs CS2 0.020. Shadow edges are blurry at 3–8 m and materials at gameplay range read as flat colour plus brick lines. Try sharper shadow filtering near the camera and slightly stronger material micro-contrast.

The viewmodel pistol's top faces render near-white and look unlit compared with the scene grade (all HUD-on frames). They do not sit in the world's lighting the way CS2's viewmodel picks up local light.
strengths: No console errors. Perf is cheap: 107 draw calls, 191k tris, 3072 shadow map, 11 post calls at 960x540.
Exposure is fixed versus r2: median luminance is 0.43 vs CS2 0.44, and crushed pixels are 1.3% vs r2's 11%.
Cast shadows are clear and readable (palms, umbrellas, lamp posts, bunting), sun shafts at mid are attractive, and the sky and clouds now sit cohesively with the warm palette.
The look is cohesive with the HUD and characters, and the overhead cine view reads well.
